newsitem.title: UK: IBCA may cut Endesa long-term ratings.
newsitem.headline: IBCA may cut Endesa long-term ratings.

text.p: IBCA, the European credit rating agency, said on Monday that the National Scale long-term AAA(n) rating of Empresa Nacional de Electricidad (Endesa), relating to debenture issues in Spanish pesetas, has been placed on RatingWatch with negative implications.
"This follows the agency's announcement on Friday that Endesa's long-term foreign currency of AA was placed on RatingWatch negative," IBCA said in a statement.
It said Endesa's short-term rating of A1 plus(n) relating to its commercial paper programme was maintained.
The debenture issues affected are the 30 billion peseta Debentures No. 16, 2001 and the 18.75 billion peseta Debentures, 2001, it said.

"The rating changes are in light of Endesa's friendly takeover bid on the outstanding shares of its two associate distribution companies, Fecsa and Sevillana in which it currently holds 49 percent and 39.5 percent, respectively.
"The cost, which could amount to some 200 billion pesetas, will be funded from internal funds and long-term credit lines," IBCA said.
